title: Best Dental Insurance 2026: 5 plans tested for cleaning + root canal + crown
description: Delta Dental, Cigna 1500, Spirit No-Waiting, Humana Loyalty Plus, DenteMax discount — same dental scenario (2 cleanings + 1 root canal + 1 crown). Real out-of-pocket cost, network size, waiting periods.
lede: Five dental plans. Same year of dental care: 2 cleanings, 1 root canal ($1,400 procedure), 1 crown ($1,200). We tracked real out-of-pocket cost after coverage, network reality, and waiting-period traps.
methodology: Same 35-year-old non-smoker, same dental scenario over 12 months. Tracked: monthly premium, deductible, coinsurance, annual max, waiting periods for major services, network dentist availability.

sections.heading: Out-of-pocket for the year
paragraphs: Total year-one cost (premium + out-of-pocket on $2,600 of dental services): Delta Dental $1,200, Cigna 1500 $1,150, Spirit Dental $1,050 (no waiting on major), Humana Loyalty $1,300, DenteMax $1,180.
DenteMax (discount plan, not insurance) saves only $400 on the $2,600 of services but premium is much lower. Net cost similar to insurance for first year.
Year-2 difference: insurance plans (Delta, Cigna, Humana) renew with same coverage. Spirit Dental's no-waiting becomes irrelevant after year 1. DenteMax stays cheap but caps out at the discount %.

sections.heading: Waiting period traps
paragraphs: Delta Dental: 6-12 month waiting period for major services (root canal, crown). If you need major work immediately, this won't cover it.
Cigna 1500: 100% preventive immediately, but 6-month waiting for basic services and 12-month for major.
Spirit Dental: ZERO waiting period for major services. The whole reason to pay their higher premium.
Humana Loyalty Plus: 3-month waiting for basic, 6-month for major. Tighter than Cigna.
DenteMax: no waiting periods (it's not insurance — just discounted rates at participating dentists).

sections.heading: Network reality
paragraphs: Delta Dental has the largest US dental network (3 out of 4 dentists). Best chance your current dentist is in-network.
Cigna network is large but smaller than Delta. Pre-check your dentist before signing up.
Spirit Dental works with a smaller PPO network — confirm your dentist is in-network.
Humana has a respectable network but smaller than Delta. Network changes year-to-year.
DenteMax has 290,000+ access points but providers vary by region; pre-check is essential.

faqs.a: If you go to the dentist 2x/year and might need a major service: yes. If you only get cleanings and have low cavity risk: probably no — the math rarely works for ultra-low-utilization.

Insurance has higher premium but caps your annual max payout ($1,000-2,000). Discount plans charge less premium but you pay discounted rates per service with no max. Discount plans win for high-utilization users.

faqs.q: Why are dental plans so different from medical insurance?
faqs.a: Lower annual maxes ($1,000-2,000 vs medical $100k+), waiting periods for major services, smaller benefit structure. Dental insurance is more like a prepaid maintenance contract.

faqs.q: Should I add dental to my employer's coverage?
faqs.a: If employer offers dental, usually yes — employer-subsidized rates beat individual plans. Check the network and annual max before assuming.

delta-dental-individual.review: Delta Dental Individual is the right pick for most adults. Largest US dental network (3 out of 4 dentists), 80% coinsurance on preventive + basic, $1,000-2,000 annual max. The default recommendation for typical dental needs.
cons: Annual max can be exhausted by one crown

cigna-dental-1500.review: Cigna Dental 1500 is the right pick if you mostly want preventive coverage. 100% preventive immediately, no waiting period for cleanings. $1,500 annual max. Strong nationwide network.

spirit-dental-no-waiting.review: Spirit Dental No-Waiting Plan is the right pick if you need major dental work NOW. Zero waiting period for root canals, crowns, dentures. Higher premium ($45-110/mo) but you can start using major services day 1. $5,000 annual max.
pros: Strong choice if you need work immediately

humana-dental-loyalty-plus.review: Humana Dental Loyalty Plus is the right pick if you stay with one plan long-term. $1,500 max year 1, increases to $2,000+ in year 3 if claims-free. The loyalty bonus is unique but only works if you're not using the insurance.

dentemax-discount-plan.review: DenteMax Dental Discount Plan is the right pick if you have ongoing dental needs and won't fit under annual max. NOT insurance — pay discounted rates at participating dentists. No max, no waiting periods, $15-25/mo.
